A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaRRR research. Their main text, algorithms, equations, experimental figures, and complete appendices support comparison across the substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original eigenvalue-estimation experiments on triple-well Langevin dynamics and eigenfunction recovery for alanine dipeptide.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D report original Langevin, non-normal Ornstein–Uhlenbeck, and alanine experiments, including time-lag sensitivity and generator-baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The Laplace-resolvent objective, trapezoidal weighting, Toeplitz construction, and primal and dual LaRRR algorithms are retained. The extension to multiple non-uniformly sampled trajectories already appears in v1 Appendix B. Newly evaluating the primal implementation does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: V2 adds an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck experiment with a non-normal 2×2 drift matrix, extending empirical coverage beyond the retained triple-well Langevin and alanine settings. This tests non-normal generators, an important part of the claimed scope previously supported only theoretically.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained transfer-operator comparator, v2 Figure 5 evaluates Hou et al.'s Galerkin projection and Kostic et al.'s Dirichlet-energy regression. These generator methods were only analytically compared in v1. Although Section 7 also mentions Cabannes and Bach, Figure 5 does not separately identify that comparator.

E3.justification: The triple-well evaluation changes from signed to absolute relative error and adds systematic time-lag sweeps using both implementations. The new OU protocol uses 1,000 Fourier features and 10,000/100,000 samples at time steps 0.01/0.001. Alanine's reported time step changes from 25 to 50 ps, retaining 250 ns training and test durations.

E4.justification: V2 Figures 2 and 4 directly test sensitivity to decreasing time lag for dual and primal LaRRR versus TO RRR. Appendix D Figure 5 adds an analysis of spurious eigenvalues from generator estimation. Neither analysis is present in v1's experimental figures.

E5.justification: The triple-well experiment reports 10 independent trajectories and fitted models instead of 100. V2 adds quartile bands across time lags alongside violin distributions, whereas v1 shows violin distributions with mean bars. The new OU experiment explicitly reports ten trials.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the original triple-well distributions with results showing comparatively stable LaRRR error as TO error increases at small lags. It adds non-normal OU recovery results and evidence of Galerkin's spurious near-zero eigenvalues. Changed metrics and protocols prevent interpreting the revised distributions as same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: V1 Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 become Proposition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2, with minimum combinations replaced by maxima in their bounds, including Equation 22. These are weaker mathematical statements, not equivalent notation. The convergence-rate exponents, principal assumptions, and most appendix derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The core claims about Laplace-resolvent learning, small-lag robustness, broad process coverage, and linear dependence on state dimension remain. The introduction broadens the empirical superiority claim from molecular-dynamics performance under computational constraints to estimation performance against TO and other IG methods.

C2.justification: V2 explains the resolvent's relevance to non-normal transient dynamics and discusses forecasting full distributions with an additional projection error. Its conclusion expands the limitations from uniform sampling to full-state observation, identifying partially observed systems as an unresolved extension.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation-and-experiments repository link, identifies Nüske et al. as the source of the two alanine trajectories, and specifies experimental kernel/feature configurations. These improve documentation; the newly identified trajectory source does not establish a change of dataset.

R1.justification: The introduction expands application positioning through graph-clustering and neuroscience references, including Klus and Djurdjevac Conrad, Marrouch et al., and Ostrow et al. Several general Koopman citations are pruned. The central methodological positioning and Table 1 comparisons remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introduction and resolvent explanation, locally reorganizes the risk formulation and approach, and adds Appendix D. The main section sequence and most algorithm and proof exposition remain, so the narrative revision is limited despite extensive visual reformatting.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column conference formatting. V2 redesigns the triple-well display as lag-dependent curves with inset distributions, adds OU and appendix figures, updates the alanine display, and introduces a full-page notation table.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially closes an empirical gap: v1 does not directly test its central small-lag robustness claim or demonstrate non-normal recovery. The targeted lag sweeps, OU experiment, and generator-baseline analysis connect evidence to those claims. Reproducibility pointers and fuller limitations also help. The reduction from 100 to 10 triple-well repetitions and inconsistent baseline attribution temper, but do not outweigh, these gains.
